heroText: Motegi works best as a base in Japan when you anchor days around Mobility Resort Motegi, Honda Collection Hall and Twin Ring Motegi Road Course. Use those sights to understand the city's history, street life and visitor rhythm. Motegi International Airport handles the main arrival flow, so hotel choice should balance the centre, transfer time and day-trip plans.

stayOverview: Start with City centre for the easiest first Motegi stay, then compare Old Town and Waterfront when price, nightlife, quieter evenings or transfer timing matter more than being beside every major sight.
hotelIntro: Motegi hotel choice is mostly about repeat journeys: use City centre for sightseeing, Old Town for a different local base, and Waterfront or Airport area when views, parking, airport timing or longer stays matter.
rentalCars: Do not rent a car for central Motegi unless parking and traffic are part of the plan; use one mainly for regional day trips.

history.label: Growth
history.text: The race was most noted for being the first oval track NASCAR race in Japan as well as being the first in which Dale Earnhardt and his son, Dale Earnhardt Jr., competed with one.

history.label: Today
history.text: Although they are separate tracks, it is impossible for races to occur simultaneously on the two courses; to access the oval track, teams must cross the road course pit and front straight.

history.label: Civic role
history.text: The road course also runs in the opposite direction from the oval; clockwise, rather than counter-clockwise.

history.label: Regional role
history.text: The course itself is built in a stop-start straight-hairpin style, which flows differently than many similarly-sized tracks.

history.label: Regional role
history.text: Train links to the area are extremely limited (the major regional lines, JR East and Tobu Railway do not service the area), nor has a planned superhighway been completed.
